title: TokenX ledger vs Ad Click Aggregator
description: Fail-closed money versus fail-open high-volume ingest. Do not steal isolation the other way.

cells.workload: Reserve / credit / finalize with exclusive terminals and idempotency keys.
cells.consistency: Ledger uniqueness. Cache balances are derived and may lag.
cells.latency: Primary round trip. Hedged writes are dangerous without keys.
cells.scaling: Partition by account with a named hotspot story. Not a firehose.
cells.failure: UNKNOWN timeout: retry same key. Do not infer rollback. Fail closed.
cells.costOps: Reconciliation, fencing, audit log. Expensive and required.
cells.whenNot: Using Redis as the ledger or ads-style windowed counts for settlement.

cells.workload: High ingest, dedupe on click_id, windows, derived leaderboards.
cells.consistency: At-least-once plus idempotent sink. Windows use event time, not offset order.
cells.latency: Queueing delay is allowed. Dashboards are near-real-time, not the invoice.
cells.scaling: Partition by click or campaign. Hot keys need isolation.
cells.failure: Fail-open admission for ingest if the limiter dies; keep unique click_id on the billed log. Shed, sample, or delay derived windows. DLQ for poison. Not money isolation.
cells.whenNot: Stealing TokenX fail-closed terminals for clicks, or treating a dashboard as billed revenue.

assumptions: TokenX is a curriculum ledger example, not a public chain requirement.
Ads can lose a window under named overload; money cannot.
Kafka copies of either product are derived unless the uniqueness store is the log.
